_comment_canonical: CANONICAL in-tree PDVD TrackFitting configuration (doc pdvd/25 sec 7b). Consumed via the TaggerCheckSTM / TaggerCheckNeutrino 'trackfitting_config_file' knob. The path IS resolved through WIRECELL_PATH (Persist::resolve, TaggerCheckSTM.cxx:976-990), so 'pgrapher/experiment/protodunevd/pdvd_track_fitting.json' works; an absolute path passes through unchanged. Keys starting with '_' are skipped by load_trackfitting_config. Values are WCT internal units (mm, us; cm^2/s = 1e-7). Read at RUNTIME: a byte-identical compiled jsonnet does NOT mean the fit is unchanged.
_comment: Forked by duplication from sbnd/sbnd_track_fitting.json; only the six detector keys differ (DL, DT, add_sigma_L, ind_sigma_u_T, ind_sigma_v_T, col_sigma_w_T) -- exactly the uBooNE->SBND porting surface. The TRANSVERSE smearing (DT, ind_sigma_u_T, ind_sigma_v_T, col_sigma_w_T) is EMPIRICAL since 2026-09-05, see _comment_transverse_smearing; the old derivation of ind_sigma/col_sigma from the SP wire filter closed form (1/sqrt(pi)/Wire_ind 5.0 * pitch * {0.3,0.5,0.2}) is WITHDRAWN (doc pdvd/42 sec 8.2/8.6/8.10: the closed form breaks above Nyquist and these keys are structurally the ENTIRE non-diffusion transverse width, not the filter term). The LONGITUDINAL term keeps the doc-25 derivation: add_sigma_L = 1/(2*pi*Gaus_wide 0.12 MHz) * drift 1.48073 mm/us = 1.32629 us * 1.48073 = 1.9639 mm (Gaus_wide is the one SP time filter OmnibusSigProc consumes; Gaus_tight is dead config). The drift speed in add_sigma_L must be the one the grouping is configured with (TrackFitting reads it per (apa,face) from the grouping, TrackFitting.cxx:6840): the PR job must pass the runner's drift_speed_bot/top_mmus TLAs (1.48073, run_clus_evt.sh). A job falling back to the 1.568 jsonnet default mis-scales this term by 6 %. Hazard: PDVD sets drift speed PER CRATE but this file is global -- if the two crates are ever calibrated apart, add_sigma_L cannot follow. Everything else is inherited from SBND/uBooNE unchanged (selection knobs, min_drift_time floor 50 us, div_sigma).
_comment_transverse_smearing: PDVD PRODUCTION since 2026-09-05 (owner decision, doc pdvd/44 sec 7): DT = 4.872e-7 (4.87 +- 0.55 cm^2/s), ind_sigma_u_T = 2.300, ind_sigma_v_T = 2.304, col_sigma_w_T = 1.176 mm, replacing DT 7.9135e-7 / 0.259 / 0.4316 / 0.0575. These are the EFFECTIVE transverse smearing of the ctpc charge the fit is compared to, MEASURED on the 120-event STM-fit arm (d42fit, 585 accepted passes): the own-centroid width of the measured profile on prolonged segments (local wire advance < 0.25 wire/slice, dead channels excluded), resolved in the fit's drift time t = (x_anode - |x|)/v and fitted jointly over the three planes as sigma^2 = 2 DT t + c^2, with the sigma of each drift bin matched to the SHARE of charge in the wire nearest the centroid (the profile is more peaked than a Gaussian of equal rms, doc 44 sec 2.3). Stable to +-0.1 mm across runs, track length, fusion state, analysis window (+-3 %) and advance cut; the SP waveform is as wide as the ctpc (doc 44 sec 3.2). The same machinery on SBND returns its DT within errors. Generator: pdvd/docs/nf_sp_img_clus/scripts/d44_make_tf_json.py from figs/44_sigma_pdvd_fit.tsv (label all, est share); arm d44sig graded against d44ref in doc 44 sec 5-6 (first-neighbour share 0.20/0.24/0.15 -> 0.28/0.32/0.18 vs measured 0.31/0.33/0.21; U_foot -14/-8/-9 %; B_foot -0.23/-0.22/-0.10 -> -0.17/-0.18/-0.09; dQ/dx vs rr unchanged). CONDITIONAL ON TODAY'S SIGNAL PROCESSING: if sp-filters.jsonnet Wire_ind/Wire_col change, re-derive from data with the two d44_sigma_fit.py commands in doc 44 sec 0; NEVER re-derive from the SP filter closed form. DT here is an effective coefficient, not the physical 7.91 cm^2/s of _comment_diffusion_superseded; the physical value stays the reference for anything that is not this fit's kernel. gaus_nsigma (TrackFitting.h, C++ default 4.0) is deliberately NOT set: at these widths the 4-sigma window no longer truncates first neighbours and a 6-sigma arm (d44sign6) was slightly worse. Known, accepted for now (owner 2026-09-05): the STM verdicts move on 311 of 1800 (event, block) pairs (98 into / 91 out of accepted), ungraded by hand; this file also feeds TaggerCheckNeutrino, whose track_fit layer has not been graded under these constants.
_comment_diffusion_superseded: [DT SUPERSEDED 2026-09-05 by _comment_transverse_smearing; DL unchanged, and this remains the record of the PHYSICAL transport coefficients.] DL/DT are PHYSICAL PDVD transport coefficients from the BNL LAr-properties parameterisation (lar.bnl.gov/properties; pdvd/stm/pdvd_transport.py) evaluated at the ADOPTED production drift field E = 0.45 kV/cm (450 V/cm, owner decision 2026-09-03, doc pdvd/29), T = 87.3 K (site default) -> DL = 4.1307 cm^2/s, DT = 7.9135 cm^2/s (4.1307e-7 / 7.9135e-7 internal). Supersedes the 2026-09-02 version (E = 0.439 kV/cm derived from the data-calibrated drift velocity v = 1.48073 mm/us at T = 87.68 K -> DL = 4.123, DT = 7.824): the field is now set directly rather than derived from velocity, and the drift speed itself (production 1.48073 mm/us, params.jsonnet default 1.568 mm/us) was NOT changed to match -- under the same parameterisation neither currently inverts to exactly 0.45 kV/cm; see doc pdvd/29 for the flagged inconsistency. Unlike SBND (doc 66 reverted to the sim pair 4.0/8.8 for MC consistency), PDVD runs on DATA in this campaign, so the physical values apply; the PDVD sim (simparams.jsonnet) still drifts with 4.0/8.8 -- on MC this file mis-models the waveforms and an MC arm must use the sim pair.
_comment_skip_revert_iso_xext_cut: doc pr/28 sec 17 round 10 (toolkit 6b219d14). C++ default -1 (off, unconditional revert). 200.0 = 20 cm (units::cm=10) -- SBND production default (inherited by PDVD unchanged) since 2026-08-06 (owner: 'overall better, please turn it on for these for SBND', gate work-pr28r10-flip vs -on48b single-event byte-identical; population gate work-pr28r10-on48b vs -off48b already on record, doc pr/28 sec 17.4 G4/G5). Abstains from skip_trajectory_point's charge-consistency revert when the point's cluster has blob-center drift-x extent below this cut -- i.e. isochronous clusters only; non-isochronous clusters (including doc pr/28 sec 13's evt 388) are unconditionally unaffected.
_comment_good_point_pitch_frac: doc pdvd/32 round 3; RETIRED to 0 by the doc pdvd/36 sec 11 flip, owner decision 2026-09-04. Per-plane floor on the trajectory END TRIM's good-point radius, as a fraction of that plane's wire pitch -- examine_end_ps_vec's is_good_point uses max(0.2 cm, frac*pitch[plane]). It existed because the ctpc is an exact (drift-step x pitch) lattice and at PDVD's 0.765 cm U/V pitch the shipped 0.2 cm radius spans 0.52 of a pitch, so an interior trajectory point passed the strict three-plane test only 17.5 % of the time against 62.4 % at SBND's 0.300 cm. The anisotropic ctpc metric (ctpc_aniso_metric, now ON for PDVD in pdvd/wct-pr-perevt.jsonnet) fixes that at its source by scaling the pitch axis by min(1, drift_step/pitch), and it SUBSUMES this floor: doc 36 sec 6 measured the metric+0.35 arm indistinguishable from metric+0 at every level (STM 653 vs 657 tagged clusters, unsupported trajectory 13.61 vs 13.51 %, and the doc-32 event's per-cluster support, coverage and cluster-109 tail identical to the point). The two must not stack. Kept as an explicit 0 rather than deleted so the production value is greppable and testable; 0 is also the C++ default, and load_trackfitting_config's set_parameter(name, 0.0) is the same assignment an absent key leaves in place (proved by hash: the flipped config reproduces the d36on arm member-for-member). Do NOT reintroduce a floor without re-reading doc 36 sec 10: the 46 cm tail it was blamed for is the END TRIM being tip-only, not the radius.
_comment_end_trim_gap_len: doc pdvd/38 shipped this at 20 cm (200 mm) on 2026-09-04; RETIRED to 0 the same day, owner decision, when unmerge_assoc became the default PDVD PR chain. C++ default 0 = the legacy tip-only trim in examine_end_ps_vec. WHY: the trim and unmerge_assoc address the SAME defect from opposite ends. scan_tip_island drops a DETACHED ISLAND at a trajectory tip; unmerge_assoc splits clustering_isolated's detached clumps into their own clusters before the taggers run, so no tip has an island left to drop. MEASURED on PDVD 039252/2 (evt 298595), same binary and same pctree: with unmerge_assoc in the pipeline, end_trim_gap_len 200 and end_trim_gap_len 0 produce BYTE-IDENTICAL mabc-pr.zip by member content (hash_archive.py e728abfe697d4cb309c9d7778dca3ea2a8155a26104fdb8ab63422adcab086a2), against a noise floor of 0 from an independent repeat arm. On the pre-flip MERGED chain the same knob was NOT neutral (stm_fit 6530 -> 5807 points, STM-tagged 8 -> 9 clusters), so this retirement is specific to the unmerged chain. SCOPE OF THE EVIDENCE: n=1 event, STM side only (-stm mode carries no track_fit layer); this file also feeds TaggerCheckNeutrino, whose track_fit layer doc pdvd/39 sec 4 reports moves MORE than STM under this knob and has never been graded. Pre-flip arm: -A trackfitting_config=<a copy of this file with 200>. sbnd_track_fitting.json is untouched; C++ default is 0, so no other detector ever saw this.
